📌 Governance Snapshots: Why Your Tokens May Not Count in a DAO Vote

Main Points
⏺ Some DAOs calculate voting power using token balances from a specific blockchain block
⏺ Buying tokens after that snapshot may not increase your voting power
⏺ This post explains how balance snapshots work and why purchase timing matters

1️⃣ Core Idea — the protocol records balances at a selected block to determine how many votes each participant receives.
2️⃣ Why It Exists — a fixed reference point prevents voting power from changing every time tokens are transferred during the voting process.
3️⃣ Example — a vote uses balances from block #1000, but you buy tokens at block #1005. Those new tokens won't increase your voting power for that proposal.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — users may buy governance tokens specifically to participate, only to discover the snapshot already happened.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — before buying governance tokens, check the snapshot block, delegation conditions, and voting eligibility rules.

Final Thoughts

DAO governance isn't only about how many tokens you hold. It can also depend on when you held them. Sometimes your voting power is decided before the vote even begins.

Talks about having talks

Qatari mediators spent more than 12 hours in Tehran discussing an agreement. Iran’s foreign minister says his country currently sees no need to meet American officials. The intermediaries are getting plenty of work.

A reported draft framework proposes transferring Iran’s highly enriched uranium to a third country or reducing its enrichment level, alongside reopening Hormuz and reciprocal economic concessions. 

No final agreement has been announced. A proposal to move the material is not confirmation that Tehran has agreed to surrender it.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who called Washington’s dialogue offer “a positive step,” says the U.S. must first accept Iran’s conditions. 

Among them are restored oil-sales waivers, access to frozen assets and recognition of a shipping route discussed with Oman, with alternative routes closed. He says mediators are discussing cutting the implementation period from seven days to two.

Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei says a newer American response indicates willingness to accept Iran’s seven conditions. Washington has not publicly confirmed that account. Vice President JD Vance’s letter to Rezaei has not been published.

The sequencing dispute remains substantial. According to The New York Times’ account of the Vance letter, Washington wants the nuclear program on the agenda from the outset, while Tehran wants relief from economic and military pressure first.

The opening of Hormuz has a proposed timetable. The opening of negotiations still requires negotiations.

Have you ever wondered why modern medicine focuses almost exclusively on chemical intervention, while ignoring the physics of the human body?

How Can You Use This Today?
